main_text.l: tivo a longum, ut, à Poeta, à musa. Verba quoq; tertij
futuri a producunt, ut, canta. Sic Antea, fruftra, infra,
supra, intra, extra, interea, præterea, ultra, a produ-
cunt. Numeralia in ginta, communem habent ulti-
mam, ut, triginta, quadraginta, quæ tamen rectius
producuntur.
Secundò excipiuntur Græca in e longum. ut, Mu-
fice, mele, gesänge / cete, walfische/ Ablativi in e, à Ge-
nitivo ei, producuntur, ut, die fide. Sic hodie, quare,
fame. Verba tertij futuri, secundæ cōjugationis, pro-
ducunt e, ut salve, manc. Adverbia in e, formata à Da-
tivo in o, producuntur, ut, belle, pulchre: sic valde,
fere, ferme, ohe, hola genug. Male vero bene corri-
piuntur. Monosyllaba hæc, me, te, se, & ne, pro non,
longa sunt.
Tertiò, peregrina in el fere producuntur, ut Mi-
chael, Daniel, Sic pol, fol, & nil, longa sunt.
Quartò, Græca in Er, quæ Genitivum per Eris for-
mant, producuntur, ut, aer, æther, character. Mono-
syllaba, far, nar, lar, ver, cur, fur, par cum compositis,
compar, impar, & reliquis producuntur.
Quintò, Nomina in is declinationis imparisylla-
bæ, quæ Genitivum per entis, inis, iris, itis, penulti-
ma longa faciunt, producuntur, ut, Simois, Simoen-
tis, ein fluß in Phrygia/ Salamis, Salaminis, ein Insel
im Euboischen Meer/ glis, ein Endhohn oder Hasel-
mauß/ lis, sauck [?] / & vis gewalt. Dativi & Ablativi plu-
rales in is producuntur, ut, mufis, Dominis. Verba
secundæ personæ singularis primi præsentis, quartæ
conjugationis, producūt is, ut, venis, ab is, nescia. Ve-
lis, malis, nolis: vis à volo, cum omnibus compositis,
quamvis, quidvis, quivis: fis cum compositis pro-
ducuntur.
Sextò, Fœminina in us quæ Genitivũ per u penul-
tima longa faciunt, producunt us, ut, virtus, tellus. Sic

page.notes: Fraktur (black letter) German glosses are rendered in bl; several are uncertain and were not verified letter by letter, e.g. "sauck" (possibly "Jauck" or "Zauck"), "Endhohn" and "Haselmauß" may differ slightly. "Mufice" and "mele" read as printed. "hola" in "hola genug" is doubtful. The Greek-looking entries are German words in black letter and are not Greek. No marginal notes are printed. The catchword "Sic" appears at the foot, right side.
